lists.name: agentDefaults
lists.note: The defaults a new agent chat starts with (Agents > Agent Chat).

rows.name: permissionMode
rows.note: acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/hub/start_mode.rs): a mode picked in a chat applies to that chat only (Leo 2026-10-21). A value MDM or the team policy forces reaches acpmux through the app's settings push (ChatSettings) and wins over the settings file.

help.text: What a new chat may do without asking. A mode you pick in a chat applies to that chat only.

rows.note: How long Claude Code keeps a chat's prompt cached. acpmux reads it at each Claude Code start (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/prompt_cache_env.rs).

help.text: One hour keeps replies after a pause cheap; its cache writes cost a little more.

rows.name: modelRouterModel
rows.note: The model the cmux model router profile (cmux) starts new chats on; acpmux reads it when it builds that profile (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/config/discover.rs add_cmux_router). The choices are the router's DeepSeek models, default first (user 2026-10-28: DeepSeek only, the 10/17 build with images by default); CMUX_ROUTER_MODELS in acpmux and the backend allowlist (INFERENCE_MODEL_ALLOWLIST) hold the same list.

help.text: The model new cmux model router chats start on.

rows.name: claudeProviderPath
rows.note: The program acpmux starts for the built-in Claude Code (claude) in place of the one on PATH. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: The Claude Code program new chats run. Empty uses the one on your PATH.

rows.name: claudeProviderHome
rows.note: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the built-in Claude Code; a bound account's own home still wins. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Where Claude Code keeps its settings and sign-in (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). Empty uses ~/.claude.

rows.name: claudeProviderArgs
rows.note: Extra arguments after the built-in Claude Code launch, before a preset's. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Arguments added when cmux starts Claude Code, one per entry.

rows.name: claudeProviderEnv
rows.note: Environment for the built-in Claude Code, over config.json's defaults.claude.env; a preset's and the session's env win. Secrets go in cmux harness secret, never this file. Not agents.env (every agent's). Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Variables Claude Code starts with. Keep keys and tokens out: use cmux harness secret.

rows.name: codexProviderPath
rows.note: The codex binary the built-in Codex bridge runs (its CODEX_PATH) in place of the one on PATH. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: The Codex program new chats run. Empty uses the one on your PATH.

rows.name: codexProviderHome
rows.note: CODEX_HOME for the built-in Codex; a bound account's own home still wins. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Where Codex keeps its settings and sign-in (CODEX_HOME). Empty uses ~/.codex.

rows.name: codexProviderArgs
rows.note: Extra arguments after the built-in Codex launch, before a preset's. Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Arguments added when cmux starts Codex, one per entry.

rows.name: codexProviderEnv
rows.note: Environment for the built-in Codex, over config.json's defaults.codex.env; a preset's and the session's env win. Secrets go in cmux harness secret, never this file. Not agents.env (every agent's). Read at each start of the provider's chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/provider_settings.rs); a harness profile of the person's own (cmux harness add) keeps its own. Empty: today's launch.

help.text: Variables Codex starts with. Keep keys and tokens out: use cmux harness secret.

lists.name: agentTools
lists.note: Settings > Agents > cmux Tools: the onboarding step's question (do agents the person starts in cmux, its terminals and agent chats, get cmux's MCP server?) and its answer, beside the card that lists the agents on this Mac, an old cmux entry in one's own config (with Remove) and the manual lines for agents started elsewhere.

rows.name: cmuxMcp
rows.note: Whether agents cmux starts get its cmux MCP server (cmux mcp serve, which carries cmux Computer Use): a Claude Code or Codex typed into a cmux terminal (the claude and codex shims, cmux-tui agent_mcp_choice.rs) and the app's agent chats (acpmux agent_tools.rs agents_get_cmux), all with one server definition named cmux (acpmux agent_tools::cmux_server) and the app's settings file. Only through the launch: cmux never writes an agent's own config; cmux setup mcp reports which agents get it and the manual lines a person runs to use it elsewhere. ask (unset) is no answer yet: no server, and the app asks at launch (OnboardingWindowPresenter.askAgentToolsOnce); on is the person's yes (it also turns the server on for these agents unless mcp.enabled says otherwise, cli/mcp/config.rs); off gives none. A Chief turn keeps its own cmux tool list either way. Rust reads it with cmux_tui_core::user_settings::AgentsCmuxMcp.

title.text: cmux Tools for Agents in cmux

help.text: Agents you start in cmux get cmux’s tools, Computer Use included: Claude Code and Codex in cmux’s terminals and agent chats. Until you choose, they get nothing. cmux never changes your agents’ own settings.

summary.text: Whether agents you start in cmux get cmux’s tools
